cases.question: How can a team organize non-sensitive repository instructions for a coding assistant?
What checks help distinguish an authentication error from an unavailable knowledge index?
Which official documentation explains how to review suggestions from a coding assistant?
Summarize the fictional team's previously discussed rollout checks without adding facts.

seeded_history.content: We are a fictional team evaluating a coding assistant on a sample repository.
Use a non-sensitive sample repository and record the configuration.
Our first check is whether repository instructions are loaded.
Keep a small documented instruction and verify its observed effect.
Our second check is reviewing generated changes.
Review the diff and run relevant tests before accepting changes.
Our third check is separating authentication failures from service outages.
Record safe error categories without storing tokens.
Our fourth check is verifying that a knowledge lookup really ran.
Use the observed lookup events rather than the question's name.
Our fifth check is that different users do not share conversation context.
Use distinct fictional users and inspect the returned behavior.
Our sixth check is preserving order within one conversation.
Measure this separately from independent-user throughput.
Our seventh check is bounded waiting for a complete answer.
Keep unfinished work distinct from a completed failure.
Our eighth check is avoiding sensitive content in reports.
Store identifiers, durations and categories, not conversation bodies.
Our final check is documenting limitations of a small experiment.
Report the actual sample count and do not infer an absolute capacity limit.
